name: The Bengaluru Uncertainty Principle
description:
What does Bengaluru have to do with quantum physics? Quite a bit, as it turns out.

This quiz will explore the surprising connections between the city and the quantum world—from C. V. Raman and IISc to present-day quantum research, homegrown startups and a few unexpected detours through Bengaluru’s history and culture.

No physics degree required. The questions are designed to be beginner-friendly and workoutable, so curiosity and good guessing will take you a long way.

name: RECYCLERS: Urban Animation
description:
What happens when a wilted vegetable, a fallen leaf, or a forgotten spoon becomes a character?

In this hands-on stop-motion workshop, we’ll turn found objects and organic waste into curious characters, strange creatures and animated stories. Using vegetables, plants, leaves, stones and everyday food-related objects, join Nikki Schuster in bringing together a  stop-motion animation—turning the inanimate to life, one frame at a time.

Please bring organic waste or any food-related items you might wish to include in your character.

name: Animated Realities: Experimental Animation and Documentary Filmmaking
description:
Nikki Schuster is the current BengaluREsidence artist at the Science Gallery. In this talk, she will present a selection of her experimental animation shorts and discuss her methodological approach to integrating experimental techniques into documentary filmmaking.

During her stay, Nikki explored emerging models of food production, urban farming, and local perspectives on soil and sustainability in Bengaluru, providing insight into her research process, fieldwork, and ongoing visual experiments.

name: QUANTUM Trails
description: Step beyond the visible and into the world of QUANTUM. Join our Mediators, Sparsh and Vaishnavi, as they trace the connections between science, art and imagination. Discover the stories and ideas behind the works and experience the many strange, playful and thought-provoking ways quantum phenomena come to life.

name: QUANTUM Trails
description: Step beyond the visible and into the world of QUANTUM. Join our Mediators, Ashi and Manasvi, as they trace the connections between science, art and imagination. Discover the stories and ideas behind the works and experience the many strange, playful and thought-provoking ways quantum phenomena come to life.

name: A Joke in Two States: QUANTUM Through Memes
description:
A neutron walks into a bar and asks, "How much for a drink?" The bartender replies, "For you, no charge!" — This joke may or may not land, but we'll leave that up to you!

Quantum physics is many things: complicated, strange, and quirky, among others. But what if we could have some fun while learning about the many mysteries of our universe? Making an exhibition on quantum physics was difficult, sure! It also included a string of shared memes, silly jokes that appeared out of nowhere and of course, one too many cats!

Join David and Sarasi from the Curatorial Team, for a walkthrough where we walk you through our experience of learning about quantum physics, but purely through memes. We invite you to look up from the doom scroll and towards our exhibition. Don't be scared of the big terms and symbols, pick up some fun facts along the way!

name: Kathegalu with Aunty Lakshmi
description:
Kathegalu with Aunty Lakshmi is an afternoon of read-aloud stories, songs, movement, and laughter for children aged 2–10 and their accompanying adults.

Across four 30-minute sessions, Aunty Lakshmi from Kadhaigal will bring Indian children’s books to life through stories of empathy, curiosity, humour, and wonder. Expect lots of fun and play rather than a sit-still-and-listen story session: children can sing, move, respond, imagine, and enjoy stories together.

This is the first event in a new collaboration between Curious Wednesdays @ Kadhaigal and Science Gallery Bengaluru’s Co-Series programme—creating welcoming public spaces to read, make, question, and explore ideas together.

name: Big Machines to Study Molecules
description:
How does quantum physics help big machines unravel the mysteries of life?

Life is organised in a hierarchy, from atoms and molecules to organelles, cells, tissues, organs, populations, ecosystems, and ultimately the biosphere. At the heart of this intricate organisation lie molecules, whose structures, interactions, and changes shape the evolution of organisms and influence health and disease. Yet, understanding these tiny building blocks of life is no small feat. It requires extraordinarily sophisticated scientific instruments, some of which are so large that they span hundreds of meters or even kilometres. In this lecture, Vinoth will explore how these large scientific machines, relying on quantum physics, reveal the molecular processes that sustain life and influence health and disease.

name: Exploring the Molecular World
description: Step into the world of advanced scientific instrumentation with a visit to the TEM, cryo-TEM, and NMR facilities at NCBS. Discover how powerful imaging and spectroscopic techniques allow scientists to visualise and probe biological structures, and uncover the intricate architecture of life at the nanoscale.

name: Meow Street Mystery
description:
We, the Three, of 13, Meow Street, host this treasure hunt and call upon your aid! O brave, capable and well-dressed strangers, might you find it in your hearts to follow the trail of our lost cat? 

Pass the trials of tricks, in this maze of mysteries, to perhaps find treasures and treats. Might you, bedecked in imaginative quantum garb, at once Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde or the Cheshire Cat alike, be the ones to band together and untangle this cat's cradle?
